original_card.question: Can the native P104 low-rank channel be completed with a legal, fully charged I-G/2 side correction?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier.

first_step.inspect: Read the P104 open next questions and its fixed local histogram; inspect why appending I-G/2 after source completion is not justified. #1991 supplies the checked native channel, not the missing correction.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one exact side-correction cut and bound its allowed cost from a favorable completed moment at a declared target. Stop or hand off if the necessary source/target access cannot be justified or even the optimistic total misses the target.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.

actual_scope: Derive a dimension-cut rank/profile capacity condition for frozen-path, X-only P104 monotone relay corrections, closing the joint-contact pricing handoff of PR2604.
scope_change_reason: Narrow the side-correction cost question to one previously unproved necessary implication after PR2604 refuted a uniform arrival-shape premise. This does not meet the complete-supplier acceptance gate.
bottleneck_link: An invalid per-helper price cannot screen a global relay design. A valid crossing-profile constraint excludes the homogeneous cheap-shape network while retaining legal individual carriers and leaves the actual complete bill open.
stop_rule: Stop after a scoped written proof, two separately implemented exact finite premise checks and failure controls; do not start relay synthesis or claim an unrestricted cost rejection.
evidence: PROOF.md and EXPECTED.json bind the written implication and all seven residual sets. Both finite checkers reproduce cut 4 = 4680. Consequences are a homogeneous lifetime floor of 4680 and at least 67 other shapes when L <= 482. Seven tests exercise the public CLI.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance in analysis, implementation, prose and separate internal proof review. No independent human or proof-assistant review.

open_questions.question: Does a complete, coupled helper-history relaxation survive the actual P104 budget after these crossing constraints and the existing departure/arrival floors?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The homogeneous cheap shape cannot provide a small network; a valid mixed-profile screen must charge every helper rather than use the refuted uniform price.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate all 256 positive rank compositions of nine, calculate their capacities at all seven cuts and retain the full paid rank histogram. Pin the candidate boundary and cost allowance before a new construction search.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package provides necessary support constraints, not geometric/chronological realizability, complete native costs or a consumer/hosting certificate.
